content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Bremerton

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP® requires a secondary degree plus documented project-management experience, or a high school diploma with additional experience hours. Review PMI's current education and experience requirements, then gather your project documentation. Eligibility verification happens before you apply, so confirm now to avoid delays.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP® Preparation course. Attend all 35 required contact hours—delivered over multiple sessions you can fit into your work schedule. Our active certified practitioners cover the PMBOK® Guide, exam domains, and real-world scenarios to build your readiness.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After course completion, create your PMI account and submit your PMP® application with your education credentials and project experience. Pay the PMI exam fee at application. PMI reviews your submission; once approved, you'll receive authorization to schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice questions, study guides, and review sessions—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your computer-based PMP® exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. Sit for the exam and receive your results immediately upon completion.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: PMP® certification is valid for three years. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) through training, volunteer work, or professional activities to renew. Plan your PDU strategy early in your renewal cycle to maintain active status and stay current with project-management standards.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.

fq_items.answer: Yes. Granite PM Academy is a PMI Premier Authorized Training Partner (ATP). Our curriculum is aligned to PMI’s current Examination Content Outline and our contact hours are fully accepted by PMI.
